sections.title: Deposit Pricing
sections.note: FDIC national deposit rates: average rates paid across insured institutions (the basis for the national rate caps), via FRED. Monthly from April 2021. Before that, FRED carries the FDIC's earlier weekly non-jumbo series (May 2009 to March 2021), averaged here to months and spliced on; the FDIC changed its methodology in April 2021 (deposit-weighted averages across branches), so levels across that break are not strictly comparable. No break is visible in 2024. Changes on cards are in basis points.

quarterly.note: Levels are quarter averages of the weekly (H.8, week-ending Wednesday) or monthly (H.6) data, $bn. YoY = quarter average vs the same quarter a year earlier. LQA = linked-quarter annualized, compounded: ((Q avg / prior-Q avg)^4 − 1). QTD = quarter still in progress (average of the observations so far; hover for count); its YoY/LQA compare that partial average with full prior quarters. Borrowings are NSA, so their LQA includes seasonal swings. H.6 'other liquid deposits' splices savings + OCDs (pre-May 2020) with MDLM. Source: Federal Reserve H.8 and H.6 via FRED.

growth5y.title: Loan & Deposit Growth: Last 5 Years
growth5y.note: Fed H.8, all commercial banks, weekly (week-ending Wednesday), seasonally adjusted, via FRED. EOP basis = the last weekly reading dated on or before quarter-end (the week used is shown under each quarter). Average basis = average of all weekly readings dated in the quarter. YoY = vs the same quarter a year earlier on the same basis; LQA = linked-quarter annualized, compounded: ((Q / prior Q)^4 − 1), on the same basis. QTD = quarter in progress (EOP = latest week available; average = weeks so far).

deposit_pricing.note: Cumulative beta = change in the product's national rate ÷ change in the effective fed funds rate (monthly averages) between the cycle points, ×100. Turning points are detected from monthly fed funds: the last month at a trough or peak before a move of at least 20 bp in the other direction. A leg ending at the latest month is still in progress.
